questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn’t want to go to a destination I already knew a lot about, and I knew very little about Finland and its traditions.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before arrival, a lot of information is sent by both the University of Helsinki and the home university. You are also added to a tutoring group with students from the same faculty. We had one tutor for Finland who helped us sign up for courses and complete the necessary paperwork. This tutoring group was a good foundation for meeting other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received assistance with signing up for courses and learning how to get around. There was one day dedicated to applying for a “citizenship” and obtaining the travel card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was offered through the university but was a 15-minute walk from campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In the end, the most important thing is that you are not too far away from your campus. It is really easy to get around by bus in Helsinki.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived at Unihome; it was fine but a bit expensive. I would have preferred shared housing, but I was assigned a studio. In the end, everyone from my tutoring group lived at Unihome, which made it easy to meet up and walk to classes together.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a lot of work with a short deadline, but everything was very well explained on the university website. The main part is to get pre-approval of courses so that you can have your OLA approved.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The host university held some online QA sessions, and was also very good at answering emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At arrivalt, it was at the end of the registration period, and almost all the interesting courses for me were already full. Some courses also suddenly changed their status from being available to exchange students to being only for degree students. It was a real challenge to get into courses, and in the end I only had 10 credits out of the 30 that would have made sense for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can’t sign up earlier than your arrival, so it’s important to consider what to do if you don’t get into your courses. I would also really recommend looking into MOOC exams, as they are easy credits that you can complete from home whenever it suits you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All master level, but I would say the courses were easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was alot of online teaching, and short classes compared to UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
In the first week alot of things needs to be paid, student union, erasmus union, gym membership eg. 
Finland is expensive, especially when traveling around.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices are similar to those in Denmark, but I would say it costs more to buy fresh food here. Student lunch at the UniCafe is €2.95, which is really affordable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
During the first week, there is an introduction to different associations, and you can find an organization for almost every interest.

I would recommend getting the UniSport membership. The classes are very nice, and the gym is well equipped.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking arround helsinki is really nice, also go to sauna (sompasauna and kuusijärvi is very nice)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a cabin trip with your friends, rent a car and a cabin. A week in Lapland is a must, whether with or without snow, Lapland is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Finns are very welcoming and pleasant people to be around.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the Erasmus events and be open to meeting new people, even if you already have your tutoring group. Also, remember to do what you want, if the people in your group don’t share the same interests, you can always find someone who does.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mainly the language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Finns are very friendly and well-organized people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go! Helsinki is a really nice city, but don’t expect too much. The university is very helpful, if you need help it is just to reach out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The university has a lot of traditions, which are really nice. But if you’re looking for a big party destination, Helsinki is not the place to go.
The Pizza in the unicafe EE is really good :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural friendships with other Erasmus students, as well as with local Finns I met through sports classes.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting into courses, and later obtaining the new pre-approval.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
